title: Node.js security baseline
notes: Docket's own curated baseline for Node and TypeScript services, drawn from the weakness classes OWASP, the Node.js security working group and the Express hardening guidance all agree on, restated as controls a reader can check. Not a published standard and it does not claim to be one: `authority` is docket. Every control here is answerable by reading a repository.

controls.title: No credentials in source
controls.requirement: API keys, passwords, tokens and connection strings must come from the environment or a secret store, never from source or committed configuration.
controls.evidence_hint: string literals for JWT_SECRET, API_KEY, PASSWORD, MONGO_URI; a committed .env with real values; config/*.json holding live credentials

controls.title: Lockfile committed and dependencies pinned
controls.requirement: package-lock.json, yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml must be committed, so an install resolves to the versions that were reviewed rather than to whatever the registry serves today.
controls.evidence_hint: a missing lockfile; dependencies specified as * or latest; a lockfile listed in .gitignore

controls.title: Install-time script execution considered
controls.requirement: Dependencies that run lifecycle scripts at install time execute code on every developer machine and build agent. The project must either avoid them or install with scripts disabled in CI.
controls.evidence_hint: postinstall/preinstall/prepare scripts in package.json; CI installing with npm ci and no --ignore-scripts; dependencies fetched from a git URL or tarball

controls.title: No dynamic evaluation of untrusted input
controls.requirement: eval, new Function, vm.runInThisContext and setTimeout with a string body must not be reached with values derived from a request.
controls.evidence_hint: eval( / new Function( / vm.run; setTimeout or setInterval called with a string; a template engine compiling request-supplied source

controls.title: Child processes spawned with an argument list
controls.requirement: External commands must use execFile or spawn with an argument array. child_process.exec runs its argument through a shell, so any interpolated request value is command injection.
controls.evidence_hint: child_process.exec / execSync with a template literal; shell: true passed to spawn; a command string built by concatenation

controls.title: Parameterised database queries
controls.requirement: SQL must use bound parameters or a query builder's parameter API. Query text must never be assembled from request values by concatenation or template literal.
controls.evidence_hint: db.query(`... ${value} ...`); knex.raw / sequelize.query with interpolation; string concatenation into a WHERE clause

controls.title: NoSQL queries not built from request objects
controls.requirement: A request value must not be placed directly into a query document, because a JSON body can supply an operator object rather than a scalar. Values must be cast to the expected type, and $where must not be used with user input.
controls.evidence_hint: find({ email: req.body.email }) with no cast; $where; mongoose queries taking req.query directly; missing express-mongo-sanitize or equivalent

controls.title: Merges of untrusted objects guarded
controls.requirement: Deep merge, clone and assignment of a request body into an existing object must reject __proto__, constructor and prototype keys, or use a null-prototype target.
controls.evidence_hint: Object.assign(target, req.body); lodash merge/defaultsDeep on request data; a hand-written recursive merge with no key check

controls.title: JWTs verified with a pinned algorithm
controls.requirement: Tokens must be verified, not decoded, with the accepted algorithms named explicitly and an expiry enforced. Accepting the algorithm from the token header allows `none` and key-confusion attacks.
controls.evidence_hint: jwt.decode used where verification was intended; jwt.verify with no algorithms: []; tokens signed with no exp claim; a secret read from a literal

controls.title: Passwords hashed with a slow KDF
controls.requirement: Stored passwords must use argon2, bcrypt or scrypt with a per-user salt and a sane work factor, and comparison must be constant-time.
controls.citation: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet; CWE-916
controls.evidence_hint: crypto.createHash('md5'|'sha1'|'sha256') applied to a password; bcrypt/argon2 usage and its cost parameter; === comparison of digests

controls.title: Cryptographic randomness for security values
controls.requirement: Session ids, tokens, reset codes and nonces must come from crypto.randomBytes or crypto.randomUUID. Math.random is predictable from observed output.
controls.evidence_hint: Math.random() used to build a token, id, otp or salt; Date.now() as an id source

controls.title: Security response headers set
controls.requirement: Responses must carry the standard hardening headers — content type options, frame options or a frame-ancestors policy, HSTS on TLS, and a content security policy for any HTML surface — and must not advertise the framework.
controls.evidence_hint: helmet() registered and not disabled piecemeal; app.disable('x-powered-by'); a Content-Security-Policy anywhere

controls.title: CORS not open with credentials
controls.requirement: A wildcard or request-reflected origin must not be combined with credentialed requests. Allowed origins must be an explicit list.
controls.evidence_hint: cors() with no options; origin: true or origin: '*' together with credentials: true; an origin echoed back from req.headers.origin

controls.title: Request body size bounded
controls.requirement: Body parsers and upload handlers must set an explicit size limit, so a single request cannot exhaust memory.
controls.evidence_hint: express.json() / urlencoded() with no limit option; multer with no limits; a raw body parser reading to end with no cap

controls.title: Authentication endpoints rate limited
controls.requirement: Login, password reset, token issue and other credential endpoints must carry a per-account or per-address rate limit, so credential stuffing is bounded.
controls.evidence_hint: express-rate-limit or equivalent middleware, and whether it is applied to the auth routes specifically rather than only globally

controls.title: User-supplied paths contained
controls.requirement: A filename from a request must be resolved and then checked to be inside the intended directory. res.sendFile and fs calls must not receive a raw request value.
controls.evidence_hint: res.sendFile(path.join(dir, req.params.file)); fs.readFile with a request value; a startsWith() containment check rather than path.relative

controls.title: Production mode and no stack traces to clients
controls.requirement: NODE_ENV must be production in a deployed configuration, and error responses must not carry stack traces, queries or configuration values to the client.
controls.evidence_hint: an error handler sending err.stack or err.message verbatim; NODE_ENV unset in the Dockerfile or start script; express in development mode

controls.title: Outbound URLs from requests are constrained
controls.requirement: Where the service fetches a URL a client influenced, the destination must be validated against an allowlist and redirects must not be followed to unvalidated hosts.
controls.evidence_hint: fetch/axios/got/http.request with a URL from request data; webhook, import-from-url, screenshot or link-preview features; redirect: 'follow' with no host check
